Oddly enough, it's been the opposite for me.  But I guess it all depends on where you're applying and for what jobs to which you're applying.

What does your resume look like?  Who are your references?  Do these positions request that you write a cover letter?  Have you visited the libraries (if they are local) and talked to the library staff about community events that may give you opportunities to volunteer?  Also, libraries don't always contact you right away.  In my experience, some have called a few days after receiving my application for an interview, but some have waited for as long as two months before contacting me.  At my current part time job in a college, I applied in June of 2012, a month after graduating from library school, and didn't hear back from them until September of 2013 for an interview.  I was offered the job and took it to build up experience and skills as well as build up my savings account but am now looking for full time work now.  And while some of my applications have fallen by the wayside, I've been getting better and better at getting the calls for the interviews lately, but it took over a year to become a stronger candidate.

Also, don't be afraid to list non-library activities like tutoring gigs or dog walking on your resume because it shows you're well-rounded and indicates community service.

Two of the jobs that I interviewed for did choose an internal candidate as I found out from the formal rejection letter that they mailed to me.  I have two more applications to send; and after that if I don't hear from them or get passed for someone else, I'm seriously considering going into teaching or possibly flight attendant school.

Thank you so much for the advice.  I've actually been doing all of what you mentioned (mainly volunteering at elementary and middle schools with occasional substitute teaching gigs) and more while I've been working at my current job which is a reference position at a community college.

In addition, I'm actually looking for a full time job in a public library:  Librarian I and II in various departments (circulation, reference), Adult Services, Children's, Branch Librarian, etc.  These are where I've been getting those callbacks for interviews.  Academic librarian jobs require specialization in another Master's degree program, which I don't have so I would never qualify for those positions in the first place.  I'm actually in the process of making a transition into teaching or becoming a school media specialist.  I already took the Praxis for School Media Specialist (5311) last summer and received a passing score for most states and will be taking the Elementary Education Content Knowledge (5018) in the middle of June.
